spots.name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
spots.summary: The Monument to the Battle of the Nations is a monument in Leipzig, Germany, to the 1813 Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations. Paid for mostly by donations and the city of Leipzig, it was completed in 1913 for the 100th anniversary of the battle at a cost of six million gold marks.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the Battle of the Nations

spots.name: Leipzig Hauptbahnhof

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Leipzig Hauptbahnhof is the central railway terminus in Leipzig, Germany, in the district Mitte. At 83,460 square metres (898,400 sq ft), it is Europe's largest railway station measured by floor area.

spots.name: St. Thomas Church
spots.summary: The St. Thomas Church is a Lutheran church in Leipzig, Germany, located at the western part of the inner city ring road in Leipzig's central district. Martin Luther preached in the church in 1539.

spots.name: Leipzig Zoological Garden
spots.summary: Leipzig Zoological Garden, or Leipzig Zoo, is a zoo in the Leipzig borough of Mitte, locality Zentrum-Nordwest, Germany. It was first opened on June 9, 1878. It was taken over by the city of Leipzig in 1920 after World War I and now covers about 27 hectares and contains approximately 850 species.

spots.name: St. Nicholas Church
spots.summary: The St. Nicholas Church is one of the major churches of central Leipzig, Germany. Construction started in Romanesque style in 1165, but in the 16th century, the church was turned into a Gothic hall church. Baroque elements like the tower were added in the 18th century.

spots.name: City-Hochhaus Leipzig
spots.summary: City-Hochhaus is a 36-story skyscraper in Leipzig, Germany. At 142.5 m (468 ft), it is the tallest multistory building in Leipzig and is beside the eastern part of the inner city ring road in Leipzig's district Mitte.

spots.name: Zentralstadion
spots.summary: Central Stadium was a stadium with a capacity of 120,000 in Leipzig which was initially used for matches of SC Rotation Leipzig.

spots.name: Museum der bildenden Künste

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum der bildenden Künste is a museum in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. It covers artworks from the Late Middle Ages to Modernity.

spots.name: Paulinerkirche

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Paulinerkirche was a church on the Augustusplatz in Leipzig. It was built in 1231 as the Klosterkirche St. Pauli for the Dominican monastery in Leipzig. From the foundation of the University of Leipzig in 1409, it served as the university church.

spots.name: Gewandhaus
spots.summary: Gewandhaus is a concert hall in Leipzig, the home of the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra. Today's hall is the third to bear this name; like the second, it is noted for its fine acoustics.

spots.name: Old Town Hall

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Old Town Hall, which dominates the east side of the Markt square in Leipzig's district Mitte, is considered one of Germany's most important secular Renaissance buildings. At the rear is the Naschmarkt. The mayor and the municipal administration have been housed in the New Town Hall since 1905.

spots.name: Paulinum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Paulinum is a university building of University of Leipzig, whose construction began in 2007. Today's Paulinum stands at the site of the old university church, the Paulinerkirche, which was destroyed in 1968 during the communist regime of East Germany.

spots.name: Augustusplatz
spots.summary: The Augustusplatz is a square located at the east end of the city centre of Leipzig, borough Leipzig-Mitte. It is the city's largest square and one of the largest squares in Europe. It is also part of the city's inner-city ring-road and a central hub for its tram network.

spots.name: St. Peter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Old St. Peter's Church is a Lutheran parish and church in the old town of Leipzig, Germany. The present church building, in Gothic Revival style, was erected from 1882 onwards at the Gaudigplatz, and also serves as a concert venue. It replaced a former building at a different location.

spots.name: Barfußgäßchen
spots.summary: The Barfußgäßchen is a 160 m (524.9 ft) long residential street in the city center of Leipzig. It connects the market with the Dittrichring and is one of the city's party miles.

spots.name: Brühl
spots.summary: The Brühl is a street in the centre of Leipzig, Germany, just within the former city wall. Until the 1930s, it was the international centre of fur trade.

spots.name: Mädlerpassage
spots.summary: The Mädler Arcade Gallery is the last completely preserved historic shopping arcade covered by an end-to-end glass roof in the city center of Leipzig. It is a facility of upmarket retail, restaurants, offices and cultural establishments.

spots.name: Zeitgeschichtliches Forum Leipzig

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Zeitgeschichtliches Forum Leipzig is a museum of contemporary German history. Opened in 1999, the museum explores Germany’s postwar division, daily life under East Germany’s communist dictatorship, and the events leading to German reunification.

spots.name: Naschmarkt
spots.summary: The Naschmarkt is a small square in the city center of Leipzig. It owes its name to a time when fruit was traded here, which was also considered a sweet treat at the time. Today it serves as an open-air restaurant in the warmer months of the year, while before Christmas it hosts part of the Christmas market.

spots.name: Markt
spots.summary: The Markt is a square of about 1 ha in Leipzig's district of Mitte, Germany. It is considered the center of the city. The Old Town Hall stands on it, which demonstrates its particular historical importance. The square was named Platz des Friedens from 1950 to 1954. Its paving is a listed heritage monument.

spots.name: Pleissenburg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pleissenburg was a historical building in the city of Leipzig in Saxony which is in modern-day Germany. It was built in the 13th century by Theodoric I, Margrave of Meissen and named after the Pleisse Mill Race which runs nearby and is often called for short Pleisse.

spots.name: Kroch High-rise
spots.summary: The 43 m (141 ft) tall Kroch high-rise in Leipzig was the first high-rise building in the city. It was built in 1927/28 as the headquarter of the Kroch Banking House, a private bank of the German-Jewish banker Hans Kroch (1887–1970), and is located on the west side of Augustusplatz.

spots.name: Moritzbastei
spots.summary: The Moritzbastei is the only remaining part of the ancient town fortifications of Leipzig. It is located on Kurt-Masur-Platz in the southeast of the city center. From 1979 to 1993 it was operated by Leipzig University as a student club.

spots.name: Coffe Baum
spots.summary: Zum Arabischen Coffe Baum is a coffeehouse and museum in Leipzig, Germany. It is a listed building in the German state of Saxony. Coffee has been served here since 1711. This makes it one of Europe's oldest continuously operated coffee taverns, along with Café Procope in Paris.

spots.name: Leipzig City History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Leipzig City History Museum, a municipal museum in Leipzig, Germany, collects, documents, and presents in its exhibitions objects, information, and contexts of Leipzig's history from its founding as a city in the early Middle Ages to the present day.

spots.name: Propsteikirche, Leipzig
spots.summary: The Propsteikirche St. Trinitatis in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany, is a Catholic church in the city centre, at the southwestern corner of the Inner City Ring Road, opened in 2015. The parish is part of the deanery of Leipzig in the Diocese of Dresden-Meißen. The official name of the church is Propsteikirche St.

spots.name: Statue of J. S. Bach
spots.summary: The Statue of J. S. Bach is a monument to the composer and Thomaskantor Johann Sebastian Bach, located near the south wall of St. Thomas Church in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany.

spots.name: Karl Heine Canal
spots.summary: The Karl Heine Canal is an approximately 3.3 km (2 mi) long artificial watercourse in the west of the city of Leipzig in Germany and connects the Lindenau harbor with the White Elster River. It is spanned by 15 bridges and is navigable with small boats.

spots.name: Alte Handelsbörse
spots.summary: The Alte Handelsbörse or Alte Börse in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany, is the city's oldest assembly building of merchants, and also the oldest Baroque building. Built as the Börse in 1678, it is now used as an event venue and is known in English as the Old Stock Exchange.

spots.name: Clara-Zetkin-Park
spots.summary: The Clara-Zetkin-Park is a park in Leipzig. From 1955 until 2011 it was Leipzig's largest park with an area of 125 hectares and was called Zentraler Kulturpark Clara Zetkin. The name was changed in 2011 and since then the Johannapark and the Palmengarten have officially been considered independent parks.

spots.name: Grassi Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Grassi Museum is a building complex in Leipzig, home to three museums: the Ethnography Museum, Musical Instruments Museum, and Applied Arts Museum.

spots.name: Südfriedhof
spots.summary: Südfriedhof is, with an area of 82 hectares, the largest cemetery in Leipzig. It is located in the south of Leipzig in the immediate vicinity of the Völkerschlachtdenkmal.

spots.name: Leipzig Opera
spots.summary: The Leipzig Opera is an opera house and opera company located at the Augustusplatz and the Inner City Ring Road at its east side in Leipzig's district Mitte, Germany.

spots.name: Leipzig Panometer
spots.summary: The Leipzig Panometer is an attraction in Leipzig, Germany. It is a visual panorama displayed inside a former gasometer, accompanied by a thematic exhibition. The current theme is "Antarctica".

spots.name: Leipzig Bach Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Leipzig Bach Museum is a museum that deals with the life and work of the composer Johann Sebastian Bach. It is part of the Bach Archive in the Bosehaus at the St. Thomas Church Square in Leipzig, Germany.

spots.name: Goethe Monument
spots.summary: The Goethe Monument in Leipzig, Germany, is a bronze statue standing on a tall pedestal on the Naschmarkt in front of the Old Trade Exchange. It depicts Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) as a young man with reference to his almost three years of study in Leipzig. It was created by Carl Seffner (1861–1932).

spots.name: Alter Johannisfriedhof
spots.summary: The Alter Johannisfriedhof is the oldest burial ground in the city of Leipzig, Germany. It began in 1278, as part of the Johannishospital in Leipzig, a leper hospital. It was later attached to the Johanniskirche, which was destroyed in World War II.

spots.name: Grimmaische Strasse
spots.summary: Grimmaische Strasse is a street in Leipzig, borough Leipzig-Mitte, and connects the marketplace with Augustusplatz. It was named in 1839 after the Grimma Gate (Grimmaisches Tor), the gateway to Grimma, which was first mentioned in 1421.

spots.name: Natural History Museum, Leipzig

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Natural History Museum in Leipzig is a natural history museum in the city of Leipzig, Germany, located at the northwest corner of the Inner City Ring Road in the locality Zentrum-Nordwest. The museum contains the insect collection of Alexander Julius Reichert.

spots.name: Barthels Hof
spots.summary: Barthels Hof is a former trade court building complex in Leipzig in Germany, located in the borough Mitte. It is the last “through courtyard” that was preserved almost in its original condition. That means, the carts drove in, the goods were unloaded, and the carts drove out - without turning around.

spots.name: Fockeberg
spots.summary: Fockeberg is a Schuttberg in the southern part of Leipzig, Saxony, southeastern Germany, and is actually a pile of rubble left over from the Bombing of Leipzig in World War II.

spots.name: Specks Hof
spots.summary: Specks Hof is a commercial building with the oldest preserved shopping arcade in Leipzig, Germany. The complex near St. Nicholas Church is an example of Leipzig's trade fair and trading buildings, which were built at the beginning of the 20th century.

spots.name: Alte Waage
spots.summary: The Alte Waage, in English: Old Weigh House, is a building that stands on the north side of the Markt of the German city of Leipzig, on the corner with Katharinenstrasse.

spots.name: Thomaskirchhof
spots.summary: The St. Thomas Church Square, Thomaskirchhof, is a square in the city centre of Leipzig, Germany. At its centre is the St. Thomas Church, Thomaskirche.

spots.name: Old St Nicholas School, Leipzig
spots.summary: The Old St. Nicholas School was the first non-church secondary school in Leipzig, Germany. The native German name is Alte Nikolaischule, the Latin name was Schola Nikolaitana. Old St. Nicholas School is also the name of a building on the St. Nicholas Church Square in the Borough of Leipzig-Mitte.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Richard Wagner Memorial

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Richard Wagner Memorial in Leipzig was unveiled in 2013 to mark the 200th birthday of Richard Wagner (1813-1883). It was created by the German sculptor Stephan Balkenhol using the base designed 100 years ago by Max Klinger (1857-1920).

spots.name: Richard-Wagner-Platz
spots.summary: Richard-Wagner-Platz is a square in Leipzig in the northwest of Leipzig city centre within Leipzig's "ring road" on the northwest corner. The square is named after the composer Richard Wagner, whose house of birth was nearby.

spots.name: Gedenkstätte Museum in der "Runden Ecke"
spots.summary: Housed in the former headquarters of the GDR secret police, the Stasi, this is an interesting museum documenting the Stasi and its methods of controlling and manipulating the people. Displays are in German; there is not much English inside. €5 admission fee includes audioguide, English available.

spots.name: Agra
spots.summary: The Agra site south of Leipzig in Germany includes an exhibition center as well as a green space with a total surface area of 190 hectares.

spots.name: Leipzig Botanical Garden
spots.summary: The Leipzig Botanical Garden is a 3.5-hectare botanical garden maintained by the University of Leipzig and is located at Linnéstraße 1, Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. It is the oldest botanical garden in Germany and among the oldest in the world, and open daily without charge.

spots.name: Old Bach Monument
spots.summary: The Old Bach Monument stands near St. Thomas Church in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. It is the world's oldest monument to Johann Sebastian Bach. Donated by Felix Mendelssohn, it was dedicated in 1843. It was designed by Eduard Bendemann, Ernst Rietschel, and Julius Hübner.

spots.name: Nikolaikirchhof
spots.summary: The St. Nicholas Church Square is a square in the city center of Leipzig, Germany. The St. Nicholas Church stands on it. The church and square have particular significance for the Peaceful Revolution of 1989.

spots.name: Promenadenring
spots.summary: The Promenadenring Leipzig is the oldest municipal landscape park in Germany and one of the most important garden and cultural monuments in the city. The term is also used as a synonym for Leipzig's inner city ring road, a traffic facility that is connected to the green spaces of the Promenadenring.

spots.name: St. Matthew

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Matthew was a church in the old town of Leipzig. During its history it had several names and functions. As a church of the Franciscan order, built in 1488, it was known as Barfüßerkirche and Heiliggeistkirche. It served as a Lutheran church, known as Neukirche, from 1699.

spots.name: Karl-Liebknecht-Straße
spots.summary: The Karl-Liebknecht-Strasse is a street in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. It connects the locality (Ortsteil) Zentrum-Süd in the borough Leipzig-Mitte to the locality of Connewitz in the borough of Leipzig-Süd in a nearly straight line of 2.5 km (1.6 mi).

spots.name: Russian Orthodox Memorial Church
spots.summary: The Russian Memorial Church of Saint Alexius is a Russian Orthodox church in Leipzig, Germany. It was inaugurated and dedicated from October 17–18, 1913, one hundred years after the Battle of Leipzig.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Russian Memorial Church of Saint Alexius (Leipzig)

spots.name: Exhibition centre
spots.summary: Leipzig has a long tradition of trade fairs, once having hosted the first and biggest sample fair in Central Europe. The modern exhibition centre was one of the major business investments and architectural innovations of the 1990s post-reunification period ("Aufbau Ost", i.e. "developing the East"). It consists of the distinctive glass hall (a landmark when entering Leipzig from the north), five e

spots.name: Bayerischer Bahnhof
spots.summary: Germany's oldest preserved railway station, built in 1842, only 7 years after the first train line of Germany had been opened. The station is no longer in use but one can still view the portal. In the course of the construction of the city tunnel the entire portal was moved away and later relocated to its original place. A new underground station is used by all S-Bahn-trains.

spots.name: Reichsgericht

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Located across the ring southwest of the New Town Hall (Neues Rathaus), the appearance of this building resembles the original look of the Reichstag in Berlin. It was built from 1888 to 1895 for the Court of the German Empire (Reichsgericht), the highest court of the Reich. During the GDR years the building served a variety of uses and hosted the Museum der Bildenden Künste. After refurbishment, t

spots.name: Torhaus Dölitz

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Exhibition of pewter figures in historically themed dioramas. The location, the gatehouse and only remainder of an old manor, was one of the hotspots in the battles of the Napoleonic wars.

spots.name: Waldstraßenviertel
spots.summary: Europe's largest uninterrupted Gründerzeit district.

spots.name: Straßenbahnmuseum
spots.summary: Dozens of historic trolleys that once ran on Leipzig's tram network.

spots.name: Auerbachs Keller

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This pub has been around since medieval times. Opened in 1525, it is among the oldest continuously operated pubs in Germany. The barrel cellar (only opened for private parties) has been the background to a scene in one of Germany's most famous plays, "Faust" by Goethe. The master of German literature himself used to drink his wine here, and the rooms are frequently the set for a live, around-the-c

spots.name: Moritzbastei & Cafe Barbakane

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very old and big student club bar and cafe. Underground cellars. Live bands or DJs most nights, outdoor films are shown in the summer. Moritzbastei was once a part of the city wall. Students dug it out in the 1970s and turned it into a club.

spots.name: Gosenschenke Ohne Bedenken

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Includes the city's prettiest beer garden but not many vegetarian options. Try their beer specialty 'Gose'. It's made with coriander and salt, and is very much an acquired taste. It is usually served with a shot of liquor.

spots.name: Riquet
spots.summary: Built in 1908-09. Two copper elephant heads guard the entrance. The interior is put under preservation and has been restored to its original glory in the 1990s. Wide selection of cakes and gateaux.

spots.summary: Dark and dirty techno club with two floors in an old industrial building in the Plagwitz district.

spots.summary: Saxon food. Large portions. Outdoor terrace, rustic cellar, or tunnel courtyard.
